title: Spiral Matrix
keyIdea: Keep four boundaries: startrow, endrow, startcol, endcol. Print the top row left to right, the right column top to bottom, the bottom row right to left and the left column bottom to top, shrinking that boundary after each side. Stop as soon as all m × n cells are printed, so a leftover single row or column isn't printed twice.

approaches.name: Peel and erase
approaches.idea: Your commented version: take the first row, erase it; pop the last element of each row; take the last row reversed; take the first element of each row going up. Repeat until the matrix is empty.
approaches.why: Erasing the first row or the first element of a vector shifts everything after it, so each lap costs extra. It also destroys the input matrix.
approaches.warn: Works, but modifies the input and the front-erases make it slower.

approaches.name: Shrinking boundaries
approaches.idea: Your active code: four boundary variables and a count; four for-loops per lap, each guarded by count < total.
approaches.why: Every cell is printed exactly once; only a few ints besides the answer.

quiz.q: Why does every inner loop also check count < total?
options: On the last lap a single row or column remains; without it, the left/up loops would print it again
To avoid an infinite while loop only
